title: Rate Limiter
subtitle: A limit shared by many servers lives in a store, and that store becomes the bottleneck
motto: A limit is only as strong as the store that counts it
coreAddition: sharded Redis counters with atomic checks
keyInsight: The limiter sees every request, so its shared store must be sized for all of them: 5 million requests a second means 143 shards, and a store that saturates fails open and stops limiting at all.

decisions.title: Start from one Redis instance
decisions.description: The first frame divides the required operations by what one instance serves, so the sharded cluster is justified by a load of 10,000%.
decisions.alternatives: Starting from the sharded design would hide why a shared counter is expensive.

decisions.title: Fail open when the store saturates
decisions.description: The failure frame lets timed-out checks pass uncounted, following the vault's advice for most APIs, and reports the share of traffic that escapes.
decisions.alternatives: Failing closed protects the backend but turns a limiter overload into an outage for every honest user.

decisions.title: Batch tokens per gateway
decisions.description: Gateways draw several tokens per Redis call, cutting Redis load by the batch size and costing accuracy, reported as the share of a limit that can slip past.
decisions.alternatives: An exact global counter never over-admits but needs about five times more shards in the sim.
